architecturalPlan.scaleRationale: This is a large, approximately 950 m² enclosed, single-storey Caribbean estate composition sized for a massive waterfront brief through one dominant living hall and two substantial accommodation wings; waterfront frontage, property limits, budget, and exact room count remain assumptions rather than area formulae.
architecturalPlan.arrivalAndCirculation: A limestone arrival walk reaches the sheltered central threshold from the south court, while the living hall opens north through a second real door to the pool terrace; the two private wings have separate exterior thresholds and use the continuous dry terrace as an open-air circulation route, with interior corridors and service circulation deferred.
architecturalPlan.volumeHierarchy: Two alternatives were considered—a vertically layered villa and a court-led estate—and the selected concept is the “Water Court Estate”: a 28 m hip-roofed salon is the primary datum, flanked by lower gabled accommodation wings that step outward without equal-box repetition.
architecturalPlan.relationshipsAndViews: The arrival sequence terminates beneath a bronze-and-timber portal before passing through the salon toward a broad shaded terrace and rectangular water court; three fitted north facade bays turn the salon toward the pool while the wings remain offset for privacy.
architecturalPlan.roofFacadeAndMaterials: Deep hip and gable roofs provide the major Caribbean silhouette, ivory enclosure is grounded by limestone paving, and bronze portal/screen elements add facade depth; screened shade and roof overhangs express climate intent without claiming thermal, corrosion, wind, or hurricane performance.

commitments.description: The primary salon is the largest enclosed volume and forms the public arrival-to-water axis.
Separate lower gabled wings reserve private accommodation capacity without asserting individual bedroom subdivision.
A real sheltered entrance is paired with an approach slab, portal posts, canopy, and the assembly's fitted door.
The terrace is a connected dry outdoor room between salon and pool, with its own shade roof and grounded posts.
The pool assembly supplies basin floor, perimeter walls, coping, and a complete dry deck circuit rather than a water plane alone.

provider.name: Water Court Estate
provider.summary: A massive Caribbean waterfront-oriented estate organized as a hip-roofed great hall between two private gabled wings, with a sheltered south arrival and a north-facing shaded water court.
unsupported: The scene is constrained to a temporary flat ground plane at Y=0; actual shoreline, survey, tides, setbacks, coastal erosion, and water-edge engineering are not represented.
The rectangular water court has an explicit basin and dry perimeter but does not model an infinity edge, hydraulic equipment, filtration, drainage, or natural seawater connection.
Exterior-designed, interiors unfinished: individual bedrooms, bathrooms, internal corridors, kitchen fit-out, furniture, appliances, and service rooms are capacity reservations only.

Screens and overhangs express Caribbean shade and weather-protection intent but do not certify ventilation, corrosion resistance, hurricane uplift, structural engineering, code compliance, or climate performance.
No automatic route solver verifies accessibility through the deferred interiors; exterior thresholds and open-air routes are explicitly constructed.
